items.answer: In: src/indicators/daysWithDelay.mjs (DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS, daysWithDelayWl) and src/indicators/delayCount.mjs (DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS, delayCountWl) with unit tests. Out: Indicator 1 and its collapsing of 2–3 (C3), any UI/dropdown rendering (C4), counting delays in 12 months (C6), other indicators.

Yes. Every option has a fixed WL: Ind.2 'no delay'→0, '<=3 days'→0, '>3 days'→2, '>60 days'→3, '>90 days'→4; Ind.3 '0'→0, '1'→1, '>1'→2. Edges from C1/C5: trimming accepted (' >3 days ' valid), other strings/case variants/non-strings → RangeError.

Only apparent differences, all resolved explicitly by the request: (a) POC dropdown text '≤3 days' vs C1 string '<=3 days' — C1 (ASCII) is binding; (b) POC AC lists WL only for >3/>60/>90 and 1/>1, while 'no delay', '<=3 days' and '0' → WL 0 comes from C2; (c) option labels look cumulative ('>3', '>60', '>90') but the caller picks exactly one option, so each maps to one WL, no overlap logic needed.
Both requirements are Must and independent; no ordering needed. They may be built and merged in any order, in parallel (one backend dev each).
items.source: Request header: 'independent of each other', 'Staffing: two backend developers work in parallel'

items.answer: daysWithDelay.mjs: export const DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS = ['no delay','<=3 days','>3 days','>60 days','>90 days'] (this order); export function daysWithDelayWl(option: string) → 0|2|3|4. delayCount.mjs: export const DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS = ['0','1','>1'] (this order); export function delayCountWl(option: string) → 0|1|2. Input is trimmed, exact case-sensitive match; non-string → RangeError. Returns a number (WL 0–4, higher is worse).

Unknown value (incl. empty string, whitespace-only, wrong case like '>3 Days', spacing variants like '> 3 days') and any non-string (undefined, null, number, array, object) → throw RangeError. No fallback WL, no coercion.

options: Frozen arrays (recommended; harmless to consumers who read/render)

items.answer: 'Trim' means String.prototype.trim() semantics. Whitespace-only and empty string trim to '' and throw RangeError. Internal spacing is not normalised ('> 3 days' → RangeError). The function returns a WL only, never the trimmed string.
